full_judgment: 2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule Nisi, in brief, are that the land measuring 41 sataks covered by CS Khatian No. 485, SA Khatian No. 16, RS Khatian No. 155 and City Jorip Khatian No. 2431, CS Plot Nos. 701 and 702 and SA Plot Nos. 1270 and 1271 and City Jorip Plot No. 7801 originally belonged to one Moimunnessa, who by a registered Sale Deed No. 4521 dated 17-5-1969 transferred the same to one Mosharraf Hossain. The said Mosharraf Hossain while in possession and enjoyment of the property obtained loan from Agrani Bank, Amin Court Corporate Branch, Dhaka on 3-1-1985 by mortgaging the said property as security against the loan. After the death of said Mosharraf Hossain his heirs redeemed the mortgage by a Deed of Redemption dated 29-3-2010. After redemption by an amicable partition amongst the heirs of Mosharraf Hossain, Md Nazirul Islam got the property in his share. Said Md Nazirul Islam sold 2.65 Kathas or 397 Sataks land out of aforementioned plots to the present Petitioner Khadiza Begum by Deed No. 4845 dated 19-5-2010. The petitioner after purchase constructed a two storied building thereon and residing in the said house. On 17-6-2012 an Officer of the respondent Bank visited the property purchased by the Petitioner and disclosed that the Bank acquired title of the property through Court. On coming to know the said fact the Petitioner by making a search obtained information from the Court concerned and came to know that the respondent Bank obtained an ex-parte Decree by filing Artha Rin Suit No. 45 of 2010 and thereafter by filing Artha Rin Execution Case No. 114 of 2010 obtained a certificate of title under section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003("Ain") vide Order No. 19 dated 20-9-2011 and also came to know that the property in question was mortgaged to the respondent No.1 Bank by the petitioner's Vendor vide Mortgage Deed No. 3562 dated 17-7-2003 as second mortgage. It further stated that the Petitioner is the legal owner of the property in question but the respondent No. 1 by practicing fraud obtained an ex-parte Decree and a certificate of title from the Court. The Petitioner is a bonafide purchaser for valuable consideration and she has right to protect her property as a bonafide purchaser without notice of second mortgage. By filing Supplementary Affidavit the petitioner also states that the property in question is situated at Dhaka District but the certificate issued by the Artha Rin Adalat, at Chittagong had no territorial jurisdiction which is in violation of the provisions contained in section 27( 1) of the Ain. At this juncture the petitioner by filing this application challenged the validity and legality of the impugned order and obtained the present Rule and Order of Stay.
